tagline: Three miles under the oaks to the town a storekeeper built.
intro: State Road 16 runs between Green Cove Springs and Starke, and for three miles of it, mostly under a canopy of oaks and magnolias dating from the early 1900s, it passes through Penney Farms. J.C. Penney platted the town in 1922 as an experimental farming village. The old trees now carry a historic classification, so they get special consideration if the road is ever widened.

The real estate slump and the crash of 1929 cut the plan down. What Penney kept was a retirement home for ministers in honor of his father, a Baptist preacher. The New Hope community dates from the same years, when Penney was experimenting with crops and the community housed African American sharecropper families.

moments.title: Penney Farms
moments.text: The visitor center and museum, the 1920s post office and a bronze statue of J.C. Penney are in town, where even the newer shops were built to match the old architecture.

moments.title: Penney Retirement Community
moments.text: The old Memorial Home on SR 16, French Norman in style, counts 24 historic buildings, built for retired ministers and now home to laypeople as well as clergy and missionaries.
